instruction.sound: England has many beautiful sights and a rich architectural history. If you are staying in London, pay a visit to the Tower of London. William the Conqueror ordered its construction in 1066, and the famous White Tower was completed in 1078. The Tower historically had many functions, including the royal palace for king and queen to reside in, a prison, a place to store weapons, and many more. ,If you're up for a trip further West, you can stop by the legendary Stonehenge. Built three thousand years before Christ, this massive stone circle most likely served as a calendar tracking the sun's movements. ,Lastly, the City of Bath was constructed by the Romans, and just like the name says, it was a place for bathing. Nearly two thousand years old, it was founded roughly in the year 60 AD and remains a stunning area of architectural history.

instruction.sound: <voice voiceLang='en' voice='f2Us_chirp'>Okay, so, if you had to choose, would you rather work in an office or from home?</voice><voice voiceLang='en' voice='m3Us_chirp'>Are you kidding? Definitely from home! It sounds so much less stressful. I would be in my own space and have flexible working hours. It sounds like a dream.</voice><voice voiceLang='en' voice='f2Us_chirp'>Yeah, but I don't think I could do that for a long time. For me, it's very difficult to focus on work when I'm in the same space that I otherwise spend my free time in.</voice><voice voiceLang='en' voice='m3Us_chirp'>I see. But as you know, I live pretty far away from the city. If I were to work in an office, I'd have to drive for at least an hour both ways every day! Even longer with traffic! That's at least two hours lost that I could spend doing something else. That's just a waste of time.</voice><voice voiceLang='en' voice='f2Us_chirp'>Ultimately, I think social interaction with coworkers is the biggest plus to office work for me. Being able to meet new people and talk to them face-to-face is very important. Otherwise, I'd just feel lonely.</voice>

instruction.sound: Australia has so many cool animals! Take the platypus, for example. This little fella lives on land and in water, and it's one of the only mammals in the world that can lay eggs! How awesome is that?There's also the emu. Of all birds in Australia, this one is the biggest. It can grow up to 190 centimetres tall. That's even taller than me!I've also always been fascinated by the Tasmanian tiger. It wasn't really a tiger, but it had stripes on its back. Unfortunately, this critter became extinct in 1936. I think we should take this as a reminder to make sure Australia's unique animals are safe and can live on peacefully.
